statement: Which of the following describes all solutions to the inequality $-3(2x - 5) > x - 13$?

choices.misconception: I multiplied only the $2x$ by $-3$ and wrote $-6x - 5$, so I got $8 > 7x$ and $x < \dfrac{8}{7}$.
I got $-7x > -28$ and divided by $-7$ without reversing the inequality sign, so I wrote $x > 4$.
I combined $-6x$ and $x$ into $-5x$ when I moved the $x$ to the left side, so I got $-5x > -28$ and $x < \dfrac{28}{5}$.

hints: Distribute the $-3$ to both terms inside the parentheses.
Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality.

solutions.reliable: Distribute: $-6x + 15 > x - 13$. Add $6x$ and $13$ to both sides: $28 > 7x$, so $x < 4$. Check: $x = 0$ gives $15 > -13$, true, and $x = 5$ gives $-15 > -8$, false.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
